bib.title: UNIFIEDQA: Crossing Format Boundaries with a Single QA System
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2020

read.skipped: The PDF ends at the references (p.1907); Appendices A.1-A.6 (hyperparameters, extended pilot results, low-data fine-tuning) are referred to but not in the PDF.

question: Can a single text-to-text QA model trained across extractive, abstractive, multiple-choice and yes/no formats match format-specialised models and generalise to unseen QA datasets?
hypothesis: The reasoning abilities needed for QA are largely common across formats, so training on out-of-format data should help.
contributions: A unified, format-agnostic view of QA and a single pre-trained QA system, UnifiedQA, that works across 4 formats (Sec 6.2) and matches dedicated systems (Sec 6.1)
Fine-tuning UnifiedQA gives a new state of the art on 10 datasets (Sec 6.3)

method.summary: Convert all QA instances to plain text in/text out with newline separators and no format prefixes, pool 8 seed datasets of 4 formats, and train T5-11B (also BART-large) on the mixture with per-dataset balanced sampling. Evaluate on seen datasets, 12 unseen datasets, and after fine-tuning.
method.task: question answering across extractive, abstractive, multiple-choice and yes/no formats

other.details: deferred to Appendix A.2, not in the PDF

models.name: Dedicated per-dataset T5 models, single-format UnifiedQA[EX/AB/MC/YN]

training.objective: text-to-text generation over a pooled mixture of encoded instances; each instance sampled with probability proportional to 1/|T| so batches hold on average equal numbers from each training set
training.hardware: TPU machines provided by Google (type not stated)

other.fine_tuning: best checkpoint selected on dev, evaluated on test; hyperparameters not given in the PDF

inference.prompting: No prefixes; input is question, then candidates and/or paragraph, separated by \n
inference.retrieval: Only in '(w/ IR)' fine-tuning variants: Aristo corpus for ARC/OBQA, 2-step IR for QASC, DPR for NatQA

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: F1 of extracted span vs gold, for extractive datasets

metrics.name: Accuracy (MC)
metrics.definition: generated text matched to the closest answer candidate by token overlap

metrics.name: Accuracy (YN)
metrics.definition: output matches yes/no; if longer than one word, correct if it contains the correct label and not the incorrect one

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests reported; Table 2 gives Wilson 95% CIs for eval-set size.

evidence.quote: we use the largest available T5 model (11B parameters) as the starting point for training our model

results.claim: On average over 12 unseen datasets, multi-format UnifiedQA beats every single-format variant.
results.setup: T5-11B trained on 8 seed datasets, zero-shot on 12 unseen datasets; single-format models trained on only that format's seed sets

results.claim: UnifiedQA beats the fully supervised previous best on unseen yes/no sets NP-BoolQ and BoolQ-CS without training on them.
results.setup: Zero-shot NP-BoolQ; BoolQ-CS 80.4 vs 71.1 previous best

results.claim: Fine-tuning UnifiedQA beats fine-tuned T5 on ARC-challenge by the largest margin.
results.setup: ARC-chal without IR, T5-11B, fine-tuned on dataset
results.table: Table 5, row UnifiedQA - FT, column ARC-chal *
results.note: Caption says margin up to 13% for ARC-challenge; with IR 78.5 vs 69.7

results.claim: Fine-tuning UnifiedQA gives new state of the art on 11 datasets per the Table 5 caption (abstract and intro say 10).
results.quote: results in new state-of-the-art performance on 11 datasets

results.claim: Pilot with T5-small: adding an out-of-format set raises NP-BoolQ from 51.3 to 59.4.
results.setup: T5-small, BoolQ anchor + SQuAD2, evaluated on NP-BoolQ
results.table: Table 3, row BoolQ + X, column NP-BoolQ

results.claim: In the leave-one-out ablation, dropping SQuAD 2 collapses SQuAD 2 performance.
results.table: Table 6, row excluding SQuAD 2, column SQuAD2

results.claim: Leave-one-out: dropping BoolQ lowers the seed average by the most (-8.4); BoolQ, SQuAD 2, OBQA, NarQA are the top four contributors.

limits: Authors concede factors affecting generalization (size, domain) are not well understood
Only 4 formats; direct-answer questions left to future work
Curriculum, distillation and teacher annealing not explored
Single run per setting with no seeds or significance tests; hyperparameters are in appendices not present in this PDF
Table 4 'previous best' numbers are fully supervised, not comparable to zero-shot
